title: Bot is firing momentum/trend signals, not mean reversion signals
analysis: Of the 4 SUBMITTED/executed trades in this journal, 2 have deeply contradictory signal sets: NVDA (2026-05-15) fired 'RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)' with score=4; AAPL (2026-05-18) fired 'RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)', 'A_GRADE setup' with score=4. Both passed the 2-signal threshold and were SUBMITTED. These are pure momentum/breakout signals — the exact OPPOSITE of mean reversion. The MSFT SELL (2026-05-18) fired only 'ADX<25' with score=1 yet was SUBMITTED. Meanwhile, 7 REJECTED BUY signals on META and MSFT (May 13-14) had legitimate mean reversion signal combinations (BelowMA20>1%, ADX<25, mild RSI oversold) with R:R of 1.68–3.70, but were blocked only because positions already existed. The bot is executing anti-strategy trades while rejecting valid mean reversion setups.
rationale: The signal scoring table in CLAUDE.md only defines mean reversion signals (RSI<35, RSI<45, BelowBB, BelowMA20, ADX<25), yet the bot is generating and acting on signals like 'RSI>65', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)' that have no defined scores and directly violate Hard Rule #6 (ADX>30 trend filter) and the strategy identity. These signals must be explicitly prohibited in the scoring rules to prevent the LLM from improvising momentum entries under the mean reversion framework.

insight.why_now: 2 of 3 actual trade executions in this 50-entry window used signals that are definitionally incompatible with mean reversion — RSI>65 and AboveMA20>1% are momentum confirmation signals. The MSFT SELL was submitted with only 1 signal (score=1), below the stated 2-signal minimum. The system is executing trades that contradict its own rules.
insight.purpose: Explicitly enumerate which signals are VALID for entry scoring and add a hard prohibition on positive-momentum signals triggering BUY decisions. Prevent the LLM from fabricating signal labels like 'A_GRADE setup' or 'PositiveSentiment' that do not exist in CLAUDE.md.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminate strategy-violating trades immediately. The two SUBMITTED momentum trades (NVDA, AAPL) should have been SKIPPED per Hard Rule #6 (ADX>25 trending on both). Enforcing signal whitelist should reduce erroneous executions to near zero.
insight.risks: If the signal whitelist is too restrictive and the market is in a persistent low-volatility regime, valid setups may already be rare. However, executing wrong-direction trades is strictly worse than missing trades.

current_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)
proposed_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)

**SIGNAL WHITELIST — ONLY these 5 signals above may contribute to signal_score. Any signal not in this list MUST NOT be included in signals_fired and MUST NOT influence the entry decision. Signals explicitly prohibited from triggering BUY entries: RSI>50, RSI>65, AboveMA20, AboveVWAP, ADX>25, momentum signals, sentiment signals, or any label not defined above. If signals_fired contains any prohibited signal, set action=SKIP.**

title: Position concentration in 2 symbols blocking 7+ valid mean reversion setups
analysis: The bot held META (16 shares) and MSFT (24 shares) continuously across May 13-14, blocking 7 REJECTED BUY signals: META rejected 3x (scores: 3, 3, 3; R:R: 3.70, 3.61, 2.61) and MSFT rejected 4x (scores: 3, 3, 2, 2, 2; R:R: 2.58, 2.69, 1.68, 1.91, 1.77). The META rejections at 609-618 had entry prices below the take_profit of ~641, implying the original META position was entered near or above current price — meaning these were genuine re-entry opportunities at better prices after partial mean reversion. The 'no add to existing positions' rule is correct in principle, but the bot is holding 2 of its 5 allowed positions in the same 2 names for multiple days, consuming the entire active slot allocation and generating zero new entries across a 3-day window.
rationale: The time stop rule says 'Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L.' If META and MSFT were held from before May 13, they should have been exited by May 16 at latest. The combination of the 3-day time stop and the no-add rule should naturally free up slots — but the journal shows 2 open positions persisting across all of May 13-14 (and likely before), suggesting the time stop is either not being enforced or the positions were opened within the window. Adding an explicit rule to log the entry date of each open position and enforce time stop exit would have freed capacity for the 7 rejected mean reversion setups.

insight.why_now: 50 journal entries show only 3 actual trade submissions (NVDA BUY, MSFT SELL, AAPL BUY) and 7 meaningful signal-bearing REJECTED entries, all blocked by the same 2 existing positions. The opportunity cost of the rejection block is computable: 7 setups with R:R 1.68–3.70 were skipped. If even 50% won at average R:R 2.5, expected value was materially positive.
insight.purpose: Ensure the 3-day time stop is enforced with a hard exit log check at session open, not just passively. Add a rule requiring the bot to audit open position ages at the start of each session and close any exceeding 3 calendar days before evaluating new entries.
insight.expected_effect: Would have freed META and MSFT slots on May 14 (day 3+), allowing participation in up to 3 of the 7 rejected setups within max-position limits. Estimated increase in active trade frequency of 2-3x during ranging markets.
insight.risks: Forcing exits at day 3 regardless of P&L may close positions that are close to target. However, this is already the stated rule — the risk is already accepted in CLAUDE.md. The bigger risk is that the freed slots get filled with the momentum-signal trades identified in Suggestion 1, so both fixes must be applied together.

current_rule: - Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L
proposed_rule: - Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 calendar days regardless of P&L. At the START of every trading session, before evaluating any new signals, audit all open positions. Any position with entry_date more than 3 calendar days ago MUST be closed immediately (action=SELL) before new BUY entries are considered. Log the forced exit with reason='TIME_STOP_3DAY'. Do not evaluate new entries for a symbol that was just time-stopped until the next session.

title: ADX trend filter threshold too loose — ADX>25 trades being submitted
analysis: Hard Rule #6 states 'If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.' Both the NVDA (2026-05-15) and AAPL (2026-05-18) submitted trades explicitly fired 'ADX>25 (trending)' as a signal, meaning ADX was between 25-30 at entry — below the hard cutoff of 30, but already in a building trend regime. The signal scoring system simultaneously awards +1 point for ADX<25 (ranging confirmation), meaning ADX between 25-30 is a neutral zone: it doesn't add points, but it also doesn't block entry under the current Hard Rule #6 threshold of 30. This neutral zone allowed two momentum trades to pass through. Additionally, 3 REJECTED META entries on May 13 scored +1 for 'ADX<25 (ranging market)' — these were the cleanest setups — while the ADX>25 momentum entries were actually executed.
rationale: Lowering the trend filter from ADX>30 to ADX>25 closes the neutral zone that allowed the momentum trades through. ADX 25-30 with rising slope is already a meaningful trend — for mean reversion, entering when ADX>25 risks swimming against building directional momentum. The signal scoring system already implicitly treats ADX>25 as non-confirmatory; the hard rule should match this logic.

insight.why_now: Both actual submitted BUY trades in the dataset (NVDA, AAPL) had ADX>25 as an explicit signal — meaning they were executed into building trend conditions that the strategy is explicitly designed to avoid. The current ADX>30 hard cutoff created a gap that the LLM exploited to justify momentum entries.
insight.purpose: Align the hard trend filter with the signal scoring system's implicit ADX threshold. ADX>25 should disqualify mean reversion entries, not just ADX>30.
insight.expected_effect: Would have blocked both the NVDA and AAPL momentum trades. Reduces trade frequency slightly in trending markets (acceptable — the strategy targets ranging regimes). Improves signal purity by ensuring all executed trades occur in confirmed ranging conditions.
insight.risks: ADX>25 will block some legitimate mean reversion entries in mildly trending markets where the trend is already fading. Some of the best mean reversion setups occur when a trend is exhausting and ADX is 25-28 but declining — the rule should ideally check ADX slope, but as a simple threshold improvement, ADX>25 is the right direction.

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 25, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. ADX between 20-25 is a caution zone: proceed only if at least 2 other mean reversion signals fire (excluding the ADX<25 point itself). ADX < 20 is confirmed ranging — full signal scoring applies.
